sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- Arvind Kumar Singh,G.A.
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1. Heard Sri Sharique Ahmed, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Arvind Kumar Singh,
learned counsel for the informant as well as Sri R.P. Patel, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

2. Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No. 123 of 2023, under Sections 376-D, 313 of I.P.C. and Sections 5/6 of POCSO Act, Police Station - Nawabganj, District - Kanpur Nagar, during the pendency of trial.

Prosecution Story:
3. The applicant along with his brother-in-law Niranjan is stated to have fleeced and fooled the victim and lured her to impart her education and subsequently, the applicant and co-accused person are stated to have sexually assaulted her and kept on doing so for a substantial period of time.

The informant is stated to have gone to her maternal home whereby she observed that the abdomen of Ajay vs State Of Up And 3 Others on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111973905/
1 her sister was bloated and when she enquired about it from her, she found that her sister was pregnant but subsequently after a period of two months, she observed that her abdomen was normal.

entities.text: Ajay vs State Of Up And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The said fact of earlier pregnancy having been terminated at the behest of the applicant was revealed by the informant after enquiring from the victim.

Rival Contentions:
(Arguments on behalf of applicant)
4. The applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case due to ulterior motive.

After thorough investigation, the Investigating Officer was pleased to file a final report (charge-sheet)
against the co-accused person Niranjan only but at the remand stage, the Investigating Officer was directed by the Special Judge concerned to take further investigation on account of the statement of the victim recorded u/s 161 & 164 Cr.P.C.,
as such, subsequently, the final report (charge-sheet) was submitted against the applicant also.
5. It is further stated that the instant FIR is just a misuse of process of court.
The applicant is a person of having low IQ and his father was having a problem of low hearing as he is barely able to hear.
His father was lured into signing the documents by certain property dealers and it is the said property dealers at whose behest, the instant FIR has been instituted.

6. The father of the informant is the co-accused in Case Crime No. 98 of 2018 wherein Manoj Nishad @ Manoj Kumar and Parshu Nishad @ Parshu, who happen to be the mediators in the instant case, are also the accused persons.
The said FIR has been annexed as Annexure No.22 to the affidavit filed along with bail application.
The instant FIR is the clear misuse of process of law.
There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 30.10.2023.

In case,
the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and shall cooperate with trial.

(Arguments on behalf of opposite party/State)
7.

The bail application has been opposed by learned A.G.A. and learned counsel for the informant on the ground that the victim was the minor aged about 17 years and she has been subjected to sexual assault by the applicant and his brother-in-law
, as such, the applicant is not entitled for bail.

It is further argued that the ultrasound report of the victim dated 21.01.2023 indicates that she carried a single line foetus of about 23 weeks and 4 days, as such, the prosecution story stands fortified.
8.
In rebuttal, learned counsel for the applicant has stated that the said ultrasound report mentioned that it is not for medico legal purpose.

Conclusion:
9. The well-known principle of "Presumption of Innocence Unless Proven Guilty," gives rise to the concept of bail as a rule and imprisonment as an exception.

A person's right to life and liberty,
guaranteed by Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, cannot be taken away simply because the person Ajay vs State Of Up And 3 Others on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111973905/
2 is accused of committing an offence until the guilt is established beyond a reasonable doubt.

sentences.text: Article 21 of the Indian Constitution states that no one's life or personal liberty may be taken away unless the procedure established by law is followed, and the procedure must be just and reasonable.
The said principle has been reiterated by the Supreme Court in Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 (10) SCC 51.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 (10) SCC 51
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned AGA could not bring forth any exceptional circumstances which would warrant denial of bail to the applicant.
10. It is settled principle of law that the object of bail is to secure the attendance of the accused at the trial.

No material particulars or circumstances suggestive of the applicant fleeing from justice or thwarting the course of justice or creating other troubles in the shape of repeating offences or intimidating witnesses and the like have been shown by learned AGA.

11. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, pending trial, complicity of accused, severity of punishment and also considering the factum of another FIR No. 98 of 2018 lodged by a lady against the father of the informant and his companions Manoj Nishad @ Manoj Kumar and Parshu Nishad @ Parshu, who happen to be the mediators in the instant case, at this stage, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

12. Let the applicant- Ajay, who is involved in aforementioned case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
13. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.

14. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
Order Date:- 15.7.2024 Siddhant (Justice Krishan Pahal)
